task:
FIX FACILITY CATALOGUE TIER LABELS AND STOP TREATING SETTLEMENTS AS PORTS (MEGA GUIDE + DAFTMAV PER-FAMILY TIERS).

Context: apps/importer/src/import_facility_templates_from_daftmav.py guesses each facility's tier from its name (_infer_tier) and marks every Starport, Outpost, Planetary Port and Settlement as a port (PORT_FAMILIES). The Stats sheet it reads has no tier column. Result: outposts and the large planetary port carry the wrong tier, hubs and the 1-yellow/1-green installations are Tier 1, and all 18 settlements are ports (so a settlement can become a body's main port and gets the specialised-port economy weight). This contradicts the Elite Dangerous Colonization Mega Guide v2.3.0 (PDF p6 definitions: space outposts and planetary outposts are Tier 1, the planetary port is Tier 3, hubs are always Tier 2, settlements are not ports; p26 tier cost pattern; p53 and p55 strong links 0.4/0.8/1.2) and DaftMav's own per-family tables (recorded in the CRE research repo as claims CL-0248..CL-0306, and in the AetherWave colonisation reference). It is defect P3 in docs/development/evidence/2026-10-21-mega-guide-v2.3-mechanics-audit.md. The workbook is not in the repository, so apps/api/src/domain/facility_catalogue_v1.json must be corrected to exactly what the fixed importer would produce from the same rows. This catalogue feeds only the planner/simulation code; it is NOT used by Ratings V4, the published Finder products, shared_contracts/ or apps/web/ - do not touch those.

Required changes:
1. Replace _infer_tier with a small pure function of the structure name, family and the row's t2/t3 CP effects, with these rules: Starport - Coriolis and Asteroid Base = 2, Orbis, Ocellus and Dodecahedron = 3 (unchanged). Orbital Outpost (all six) = 1. Planetary Port - the large 'Port' (id planetary_port) = 3; 'Outpost Civilian/Industrial/Scientific' = 1. Hub (all nine) = 2. Installation = 2 if it costs Tier 2 points (t2_cp_effect < 0: Government, Medical, Military, Research Station, Security Station, Space Bar, Tourist), otherwise 1 (Comm Station, Mining Outpost, Pirate Base, Relay Station, Satellite, Space Farm). Settlement = keep the size label in the name ('T1 S'/'T1 M' = 1, 'T2 L' = 2; unchanged). Keep a conservative fallback for unknown families.
2. Settlements are not ports. Remove 'Settlement' from PORT_FAMILIES and from the families that get category 'port': all 18 settlements get is_port false, is_support_facility true, and a category from their economy by the same rule hubs and installations already use. Keep their ids, names, costs, generated points, prerequisites and unlocks unchanged.
3. strong_link_value keeps following tier (0.4/0.8/1.2) as the importer already does.
4. Update facility_catalogue_v1.json by applying the corrected importer functions to every existing DaftMav entry (use each entry's source_structure and stat_effects.source_fields; do not hand-type values), then re-sort and serialise exactly as the importer does (sort key (allowed_location, category, tier, name); json.dumps indent=2, sort_keys=True, trailing newline). Only tier, is_port, is_support_facility, category and strong_link_value may change, plus template order where the sort key changed. Do NOT change any cost or generated value. In particular leave the small/medium Research Bio settlements at cost 1 yellow / gives 1 green: other sources say free / gives 1 yellow, which is an open in-game question for a separate change. Expected changes: 6 orbital outposts tier 2->1 (link 0.8->0.4); 3 planetary outposts tier 2->1 (0.8->0.4); planetary_port tier 2->3 (0.8->1.2); 9 hubs tier 1->2 (0.4->0.8); 7 installations tier 1->2 (0.4->0.8); 18 settlements is_port true->false. The colony_ship bootstrap entry is unchanged.
5. In apps/api/src/mechanics/cp_rules.py keep ESCALATING_PORT_TIER_BY_ID and NON_ESCALATING_PORT_IDS unchanged as an explicit guard, but correct the comment that says the catalogue labels those 15 as Tier 2 ports.
6. Do not change is_colony_port (separate task), API response shapes, field names or OpenAPI output; do not edit Ratings V4 files, shared_contracts/, sql/, apps/web/ or frontend/.

Tests (pytest, no database):
(a) Unit tests for the importer's tier, port, support and category functions using synthetic row data covering every family and rule above (no workbook needed).
(b) A consistency test: for every DaftMav entry in facility_catalogue_v1.json, recomputing tier, is_port, is_support_facility, category and strong_link_value from source_structure and stat_effects.source_fields with the importer's functions equals the stored values, and the stored template order equals the importer's sort order. This proves the JSON is what the importer would write.
(c) In tests/test_facility_catalogue.py assert representative corrected values: orbital_outpost_civilian tier 1 link 0.4; surface_planetary_port_outpost_civilian tier 1; planetary_port tier 3 link 1.2; refinery (hub) tier 2 link 0.8; orbital_installation_medical tier 2; orbital_installation_satellite tier 1; surface_settlement_agriculture_t1_s tier 1 is_port false is_support_facility true; surface_settlement_agriculture_t2_l tier 2 is_port false; surface_settlement_research_bio_t1_s still cost 1 yellow / gives 1 green.
(d) Behaviour tests with the bundled catalogue through the topology graph or simulate_build_preview: on one rocky body with a Coriolis primary port, a refinery hub and a small agriculture settlement both strongly link to the Coriolis (hub 0.8, settlement 0.4) and neither is a main port; a body with only a settlement and a hub has no main port and produces no strong links; on a body where a civilian orbital outpost is built before a Coriolis, the Coriolis is the main orbital port.
Update existing tests that relied on settlements being ports or on the old tiers so they assert the new contract (likely tests/test_topology_graph.py, tests/test_facility_catalogue.py, tests/test_cp_escalation_guide.py, and any optimiser, planner, recommendation or golden-scenario test that uses the bundled catalogue). Never delete or weaken an assertion just to make it pass; explain each test change in your summary. Run ruff on touched files and pytest on every test file that imports the facilities domain, the bundled catalogue, the importer, topology_graph, build_preview, port_economy, the optimiser or recommendations. In your summary list every changed template id with old -> new values.
